The Cultural Allianceâ€™s work falls into two primary pillars: awareness & access and audience engagement. Access broadens the vision of what the arts do for the community and make sure support for the sector is as efficient and effective as possible. Through audience engagement, the Alliance serves as a critical connector between the arts and the general public to broaden cultural participation and to maximize the earned revenue that partially sustains these activities.

The Unity Performing Arts programming is focused on the goal of developing young people in the areas of character, artistry, and leadership. UNITY's  innovative approach showcases non-traditional soulful art forms that bring cultural relevance to the community and diversity among artists, artistry and audiences. Embedded within all UNITY programming are experiences to develop natural talents, enhance social-emotional skills, build character, and develop leadership and 21st Century skills.

ChiS&E  provides a rigorous  4 week  summer enrichment curriculum with intentional connections between algebraic/calculus concepts and skills students need into computer science and engineering courses through promoting 21st century skills, innovative technology use, and lifelong learning. The Raspberry Pi curriculum encourages students to become familiar with basic computer programming and apply coding techniques and skills to design a final product: Python, C/c++, Java.

CodePath.org offers a three-part program that reinforces fundamentals to better prepare students for the technical interview as well as job performance. Students complete an assessment that gauges their technical mastery levels and job application readiness and matches them to their appropriate course level along with a personalized action plan.\\This programâ€™s goal is to improve student interview preparedness by an average of 20% year over year and bridge the CS Fundamentals gap.

The Baltimore Educational Scholarship Trust, in partnership with our eighteen independent member schools, recruits and supports through the admissions process academically talented African American students with financial need from the Baltimore area. Once students are enrolled, B.E.S.T. positions them for success through academic preparation, leadership development, and support programs.

Y.O.U.'s Out-of-School Time (OST) Program provides free, high-quality learning, social-emotional enrichment, and trauma-informed support services for 1,000 youth each year across 11 schools in Evanston and Niles Townships.\\The OST Program offers a â€œhigh expectations, high supportâ€ pathway to post-secondary and life success. Y.O.U.'s model helps youth to grow in four areas: skills and knowledge, self-regulation, mindsets, and values.

We are a pro bono legal services agency dedicated to helping low-income people in Northeast Indiana. Founded in 2002, we provide equal access to the civil justice system for disadvantaged residents by facilitating direct referrals to attorney volunteers who represent individuals without charge in a wide variety of civil legal matters.

Cedars Hope is a permanent, supported housing program for homeless women facing chronic and severe mental illness. Residents live in a group style setting and receive person-centered support in order to build skills, self-confidence, and self-reliance, with the ultimate goal of living independently again. Supportive services include case management, advocacy, goal-setting, transportation, and additional aftercare support up to 6 months after moving out. Cedars Hope can house up to 16 residents at a time.

Junior Achievement's programs center on the pillars of financial literacy, entrepreneurship and work readiness.  Junior Achievement helps K-12 grade students connect education with their future success. Programs are delivered by volunteers in schools over a 5-8 week depending on grade level.

Prepped! enables underserved, low income, and first-generation college-bound youth to build a path toward career success through tailored career readiness training, paid work experience, and college- and career-counseling. Prepped! helps more than 300 teens annually to learn critical employment skills and develop the tools they need to graduate from the program confident and prepared to enter the workforce.

Rapid Rehousing is HUD model program and the National Alliance to End Homelessness reports it is effective in helping people to quickly exit homelessness, prevent persons from returning to homelessness, increase people's self-sufficiency, and is more cost-effective than other methods such as shelter. Fast Track involves a thorough assessment, intensive housing-focused case management, and temporary financial assistance including rent, utilities, and moving costs. The program is designed to provide the minimum necessary for housing stability.

Per Scholas Newark prepares un/underrepresented individuals for thriving careers in tech through a variety of training tracks that lead to industry-recognized credentials in fields like Software Engineering, IT Support, Cybersecurity and AWS. The cohort-based, boot camp-style training tracks are offered full-time for 12-15 weeks on a rolling basis and lead to potential employment opportunities with partnering employers facilitated by a dedicated Business Solutions team member.

The Economic Empowerment Program of New Hampshire support the growth and development of economic justice initiatives statewide to survivors of domestic and sexual violence.  Advocates at the 13 crisis centers administer financial literacy programming to survivors in one-to-one and in workshop settings.  The program provides an asset-based tool, a matched savings program, to survivors who participate in financial literacy programming.

In 2015, the Academy launched a virtual program for the worldâ€™s brightest and most STEM-motivated students aged 13-17 â€“ The Junior Academy. It is a passionate community of problem solvers made up of talented students, STEM experts, and companies around the world dedicated to designing innovative solutions to global challenges. Throughout the program, students apply their STEM and 21st century skills to solve real-world problems related to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Ohio provides children with positive mentoring relationships that help youth develop trust, build their self-confidence and increase their social-emotional skills. \\* Community-based Mentoring matches caring adult Big Brothers or Big Sisters in individual mentoring relationships with children in need of adult friendship and guidance.  \\* School-based Mentoring matches positive adults in individual mentoring relationships with children at more than thirty schools around central Ohio.

YMCA START is a research-based, structured, educational enrichment after-school program for students in grades K-5 that utilizes prescribed dosages of educational components and meets strict fidelity markers. Y-START fills a critical need within the city of Manchester as it is specifically designed to provide a safe, enriching program for over 140 low-income children living in a neighborhood where they can be touched by violence and/or drugs on a daily basis.

The CT YOUTH Forum (CYF), a program of The CT Forum, reduces racial/socio-economic isolation, breaks stereotypes and provides experiential learning for hundreds of high school youth from 35 schools all over CT who meet throughout the year for issue-focused discussion and activities that include youth planning and participating in large and small group issue-focused discussions, held monthly in member schools, facilitated by students and CYF staff.

The Literacy Initiative engages youth in multi-sensory instruction and enrichment after school using techniques incorporating auditory, visual, and kinesthetic learning to boost phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, comprehension, and vocabulary. Through this program, participants take part in encoding and decoding practice while working towards independent reading and writing. As a result of participation, we expect participants to increase their basic literacy skills, build confidence, and develop into life-long learners.

The YMCA Achievers Program is data-driven and strategically designed to develop individual talents and leadership skills, and prepare teens for life beyond high school. With a focus on 8th-12th graders, our goal is to support high school graduation, prepare teens for college and begin exploring career possibilities. Example activities: Career Exploration; Leadership; Mentoring; Cultural Enrichment; SAT Preparation; College Tours; Teen Summit

Through the Senior Year Success Series program, Embarc provides high school seniors with high-impact experiential learning experiences. Throughout the year, experiences include: overnight college trips, career fairs, financial literacy workshops and post-graduation preparation. The Senior Year Success Series aims to equip students with the skills and resources needed for postsecondary success and to realize all that is possible in their bright futures.

In summer 2019, BellXcel will deliver our education program to 300 Baltimore scholars, grades K-5, at 3 community schools. For 6 hours a day, 5 days per week, over 5 weeks, scholars will grow literacy, math, social, and emotional skills through daily academic instruction, 21st Century enrichment courses, community time, community guest speakers, and field trips. We aim to: a) help scholars achieve on average at least one month of academic skills, b) strengthen self-confidence for 75% of scholars, and c) increase engagement for 75% of parents.

The Foundationâ€™s core financial aid program provides interest-free, fee-free loans and outright grants to students for post-secondary education. The Foundation provides funding to qualified low-income students who are pursuing graduate, bachelors, associate, and technical degrees at accredited educational institutions throughout the United States. Every student funded by the Foundation is assigned to a Student Advisor who monitors their progress and provides support as needed throughout their college experience.

Working on Womanhood (WOW) is a multifaceted school year long group counseling and therapeutic mentoring program that works to improve the social emotional and behavioral competencies for 7-12th grade girls exposed to traumatic stressors and/or with emotion regulation challenges. WOW participants increase their school engagement and achievement, decrease aggression, and improve their psychological well-being.

Working on Womanhood (WOW) is a multifaceted school year long group counseling and therapeutic mentoring program that works to improve the social emotional and behavioral competencies for 7-12th grade girls exposed to traumatic stressors and/or with emotion regulation challenges. WOW participants increase their school engagement and achievement, decrease aggression, and improve their psychological well-being.

Family Promise of Greater Orlando is partner in a collaborative rapid rehousing project for families experiencing homelessness within Orange County, Florida.  Family Promise provides housing stability case management services to help homeless families who qualify for rapid rehousing rental assistance identify, rent, set up and maintain stable housing.

Leadership Academy is an intensive year-long professional learning program that offers arts educators an opportunity to collaborate with a close network of peers who are devoted to becoming leaders in their schools and organizations. Participants deeply explore issues of leadership and child-centered learning--with a special focus on culturally relevant arts education--through facilitated discussions, activities, and arts experiences and developing and carrying out a self-directed action plan related to their professional goals.

Our After-School Adventures program is a tutoring and gaming program at three branches of the Orange County Library System. The program is free and provides homework help to students 11 and up, then unwind and get creative with our imaginative role-playing games and strategic board games. During the program, students learn the importance of teamwork, strategy, and a variety of social skills.

Breakthrough's summer violence prevention programs serve over 4,000 local East Garfield Park residents each year by reclaiming public spaces for safety and promoting events that reduce violence. Events are held throughout the summer in neighborhood "hot spots" that have been identified by community stakeholders and in partnership with the University of Chicago Crime Lab. At these locations, residents gather to participate in fun activities that support healthy living and freedom from violence.

TrustPlus is Neighborhood Trustâ€™s worker financial health benefit: live, human-touch financial coaching, delivered via phone/video, and linked to goal-oriented products. Financial Coaches enable clients to take action so they can reduce debt and save. As a national social enterprise, TrustPlus reaches workers through over 180 SMBs, fintechs and benefits networks. In 2020, TrustPlus helped struggling workers survive income loss by pioneering an inclusive cash relief + financial coaching model.

Many children are struggling to read on grade level by the end of third grade and are not deemed proficient readers through state testing. This is especially true of students from low income communities who have not been read to or exposed to preschool and books are at a disadvantage. ReadingPals is a tutoring and mentoring program that aims to improve students reading levels and social emotional health. We also aim to provide a positive association with literacy and develop at home libraries, through the provision of take-home books. Pairing a student up one-to-one with a volunteer ReadingPals allows them to receive the benefits of tutoring and mentoring alike.

LeadersUp bridges the talent divide by creating an Opportunity Marketplace where talent supply and demand intersect to create an antiracist economy that positions the next generation of BIPOC talent at the center of our nation's economic recovery and growth.  LeadersUp partners with employers to provide in-demand career readiness training and coaching for young adults to accelerate their education-to-employment outcomes, increase economic mobility and expand life-long wealth creation/well being.

GNEC's  MWDB Business Enhancement Program consists of providing business counseling, consulting and financing to the MWDBs. The program consists of both classroom workshops and individualized technical assistance to entrepreneurs in completing and  implementing a  business plan,and providing assistance in accessing technology and financing. More specifically, the Program provides a entrepreneurial training model that presents essential tools and concepts for managing any business in a simplified yet practical way

The  Opportunity Youth Network Program is designed to reengage youth who have separated from school before graduating, help them earn a high school diploma and transition them into post-secondary or employment opportunities.

Big Brothers Big Sisters mentor2.0 is designed to help students considered most at-risk graduate from high school prepared for the future â€“ socially, academically, and professionally.  mentor2.0 leverages specific curriculum and email communication with in-person events to reach high school students through a technology-driven program that is more flexible on the mentorâ€™s and menteeâ€™s schedule.  Results are impressive with 97% of mentor2.0 graduates enrolling in college, enlisting in the military or gaining employment.

mentor2.0 focuses on matching students from low-income areas in a positive one-on-one relationship with college-educated mentors. The goal of these relationships is to equip low-income students to graduate high school, succeed in college, and achieve their future ambitions. Unlike our traditional programming, mentor2.0 interactions and conversations occur via an online platform.

Horses & Heroes program is an equine-assisted therapy program for post-9/11 Veterans suffering with PTSD. A group of approximately 10 Veterans meets for 12 weeks, 3 hours a week for group therapy with a licensed mental health counselor and they participate in both mounted and unmounted activities with the horses and a certified equine specialist/riding instructor.

WPDN provides care and education for children ages 6 weeks to 5 years old 5 days per week to engage, support and educate the youngest citizens so they are prepared for Kindergarten and beyond. Students who attend WPDN's high-quality preschool program are better prepared for kindergarten than children from similar backgrounds, who did not have the benefit of attending such a high quality preschool program. By focusing on relationships, social emotional skills, and initiative, WPDN prepares students for success in school and in life.

The Orlando International Fringe Theatre Festival is a 14-day performing arts festival that offers over 1,000 live stage productions across 14 indoor theatrical venues, an outdoor stage, and non-traditional performance spaces. Over 130 performing groups and individual artists are selected through a lottery to participate for this international celebration of theatre, dance, music and arts. Tickets range from free to $12 with 100% of the ticket proceeds going directly to the artists.

YWCA After School STEM programs offer focused attention in math to school age children primarily in grades K-5 at local area public schools. Instruction is offered in an informal setting, from highly qualified tutors during both the Fall and Spring academic terms, and during intersession, spring and summer breaks. Participants who engage with the curriculum will demonstrate improved grades in math, as well as attitudinal changes toward math to include increased interest and reduced anxiety--measured through collection of grades and surveys.

Braven supports underrepresented students from college to career by partnering with universities and employers to offer a two-part experience that begins with a credit-bearing college course followed by a post-course experience that lasts through graduation. Fellows emerge from Braven with the skills, experiences, confidence and networks they need to land a strong first job and get on a path to economic freedom.

Year Up's mission is to close the Opportunity Divide by ensuring that young adults gain the skills, experiences, and support that will empower them to reach their potential through careers and higher education. We deliver a six-month employment-training curriculum specifically focused on tools needed to excel in today's job market coupled with a corporate internship that prepares young adults for entry-level roles at some of leading employers, as well as a pathway toward continued higher education.

Bookmark Buddies is a successful literacy program designed to raise the\reading levels of at-risk third grade students read below grade level and are\at risk of scoring a Level 1 on the FSA. To improve reading skills and\reduce the risk of retention, Bookmark Buddies matches these third grade\students with trained mentors from the community. Once matched, the\they meet once a week for thirty minutes in the childâ€™s school\using carefully selected reading materials at the childâ€™s current reading\level, assessing them throughout to track progress.

MANNAâ€™s Food is Medicine model provides its critically ill clients with the nutrition necessary for their medical treatments to be successful. MANNAâ€™s evidence-based program improves health and quality of life by providing individually tailored medical nutrition and professional nutrition counseling as essential parts of medical treatment. MANNA delivers complete nutrition to each clientâ€™s doorâ€”21 meals per week, including fresh fruit and healthy dessertsâ€”and provides ongoing professional nutrition counseling with its registered dietitians.

Interval House operates a Safe House for victims of domestic violence; individuals, and families with children that do not have any other safe alternatives or resources. In a secure and confidential location, Interval House's trained advocates deliver ongoing support and basic needs services 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Adult and child participants have the opportunity to identify current challenges and develop strategies to overcome barriers as they start to rebuild from the crisis and violence that has impacted their lives.

The Resource Foundation will collaborate with local partner Instituto Perene to implement this program, which seeks to substitute rudimentary wood burning stoves with Pereneâ€™s improved cookstove model in Reconcavo (Bahia, Brazil). Stoves reduce use of firewood as fuel, and curb deforestation and greenhouse emissions. Furthermore, local women are trained on their use and maintenance, thereby advancing indicators outlined in SDG 1 (End Poverty), SDG 7 (Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Change).

The Smart Duka Initiative aims to enhance the profitability of micro retail shops in Kenya. Through comprehensive training and mentorship, the program focuses on improving financial management, operational efficiency, marketing, and digital adoption. Additionally, the initiative fosters business formalization by creating business groups and addresses regenerative sustainability through waste management strategies.

Seeking to increase diversity in debate and advocacy, close the extracurricular opportunity gap, and increase literacy in Baltimore city students, the Baltimore Urban Debate League partners with schools to provide afterschool competitive debate programs across the 45 of the cityâ€™s elementary, middle, and high schools.  Tournaments occur throughout the school year and all students have to debate both sides of the topic throughout the day.

The Summer Arts & Learning Academy is a full-day, six-week program to prevent summer learning loss. It is provided at no cost to Baltimore City Public School elementary students. During the program, students are instructed by professional artists and teachers who co-plan and co-teach math and literacy lessons through a variety of art forms - from slam poetry and ceramics to drama, percussion, and dance.

The Summer Arts & Learning Academy is a full-day, six-week program to prevent summer learning loss. It is provided at no cost to Baltimore City Public School elementary students. During the program, students are instructed by professional artists and teachers who co-plan and co-teach math and literacy lessons through a variety of art forms - from slam poetry and ceramics to drama, percussion, and dance.

Middle Grades Partnership is a three-year program for academically promising Baltimore middle school students that provides educational opportunities, enriching experiences, and access across social boundaries through partnerships with area public and private schools. 150-hours of summer programming, five full days a week over five weeks, gives students the opportunities that ensure summer learning gains.

The Ingenuity STEM Talent Pipeline Expansion focuses on improving and expanding the pipeline of talented STEM leaders in Baltimore City from underserved communities. The overall aim is to increase the number of low-income students served and retained in our program from 37.5% to 55 percent by 2019-20.

Higher Achievement works to close the opportunity gap during the pivotal middle school years by providing students with academic and social-emotional supports. Scholars partake in rigorous academic out-of-school time programming. They receive homework help and curricular instruction; participate in hands-on elective courses and service-learning projects; and work with volunteer mentors twice per week. Higher Achievement then ensures scholars matriculate high schools that can provide the support they need to stay on the trajectory to college.

SBLC, an adult literacy organization enrolling 700 learners a year, offers 3 paths to a high school diploma: ABE/GED classes offered in 3 academic sessions, National External Diploma Program (NEDP) offered year-round, and iPathways (online program). SBLC also provides a yer-round Tutoring Program; Bridge Programming; and a Career Transition Program that includes integrated education/training,career pathway planning, and cooperative education for all grade levels. SBLC uses a partnership model to provide support to aid in retention.

Big Brothers Big Sisters at the Y (BBBSY) is a one-to-one, professionally supported mentoring program for youth ages 7-17 designed to provide consistent, caring, positive role modeling and supportive guidance. Mentoring takes place across central Maryland, serving over 800 children living in under-resourced communities. (82% of mentored children live in the Baltimore area.) Matches meet regularly to engage in healthy, positive activities which lead to trusting, long-term relationships that build mentees confidence and self-esteem.

Camp St. Vincent (CSV) is a free, all-inclusive, full-day camp for homeless children ages 5-14. It is staffed with counselors who implement a curriculum that helps children overcome the damaging effects of homelessness. The curriculum includes reading, math, and social-emotional components that address summer learning loss and build resiliency skills. CSV also provides a fun, holistic camp experience by providing art, dance, nature exploration, water safety instruction, and weekly field trips.

It is staffed with counselors who implement a curriculum that helps children overcome the damaging effects of homelessness. The curriculum includes reading, math, and social-emotional components that address summer learning loss and build resiliency skills. CSV also provides a fun, holistic camp experience by providing art, dance, nature exploration, water safety instruction, and weekly field trips.

Girl Scouts of Central Maryland, Inc. adapts the four pillars of Girl Scouting (GS)  into a program delivered to girls in four Baltimore City Title 1 schools.  These pillars are: STEM, social skills, entrepreneurship and the outdoors.  Using GS principles of "discover, connect, take action" GSCM will deliver a series of sessions to girls in grades K-8.  Girls will acquire knowledge and skills to: start their own cookie business, compete in a GS Robotics Expo, engage in healthy behaviors - physical and social, and plan a service project.

The Prodigy Program and CodeWorks are advanced job skills education and mentoring programs.  Through CodeWorks youth are paid to attend a 5-6 week full-time summer program in which they learn high level programming languages and meet and interact with industry professionals. In the Prodigy Program, which takes place after school during the school year, youth receive further job skills and technical training as well as 21st century skills such as communication, collaboration, and problem solving.

Power Project (PP) is a successful after school program for children and families living below the federal poverty line in Reservoir Hill & Penn North (RH/PN). Launched in 2009, we have seen literacy increase from 2-5 grade levels, and more than 70% of our youth have a "B" or better average on their report cards. PP consists of three major components: education, mentoring, the arts, and human services.PP is at no cost to youth and families and is held at the Center Monday through Thursday from 3:00 to 6:15 pm.

Readers to Leaders is an evidence-based, national award-winning program focused on strengthening literacy skills in Club youth. Readers to Leaders is adaptive and results-driven, fit for younger members ages 6-12. The Clubsâ€™ Readers to Leaders program is divided between Lalilo Readers and STAR Readers. When Lalilo Readers complete programming and achieve their goals, they transition to STAR Reading. While the Omaha Community Foundation reports third-grade students in Douglas and Sarpy counties are less proficient at reading (34%) compared to their neighbors in Pottawattamie County (69%), the Clubsâ€™ Readers to Leaders program teaches important reading skills necessary to connect with and understand text.

The Extended Learning Opportunity program provides support to help students become successful in school and in life. To do so the program provides children with supplemental academic and social development skills outside of the traditional school day.  This community-based program, held afterschool during the school year and full days in the summer, offers tutoring, homework assistance, Social Emotional Learning lessons, STEM activities, enrichment, and literacy-focused activities for low income and/or minority children and their parents.

MLK Montessori offers a high-quality Montessori program that is specifically designed to meet the unique needs of at-risk, low-income preschool and kindergarten children. The school's goal is to help these children develop the skills they need to keep pace with their peers from more advantaged environments and achieves success in school. MLK ensures that all students, regardless of their income, have access to the program by offering student scholarships and by working closely with both the Child Care Development Fund and On My Way PreK.

This program prepares pre-k students at two early learning centers for kindergarten. Components of this program include direct education and care services for approximately 100 pre-k students (who are not a part of the On My Way pre-k program), the remaining children who are part of the On My Way pre-k program, and family engagement for their parents/guardians. With the quality education our pre-k students receive and the reinforcement from parent engagement, our pre-k students will graduate from our learning centers prepared for their kindergarten year. This impacts the child's success in school and beyond.

With the quality education our pre-k students receive and the reinforcement from parent engagement, our pre-k students will graduate from our learning centers prepared for their kindergarten year. This impacts the child's success in school and beyond.

Completely KIDS provides after school programming at thirteen locations for more than 2,000 youth each year. Programming targets school-aged children living in poverty and provides them with access to healthy food, academic assistance, enrichment experiences, and family support to overcome barriers to success. Program outcomes highlight achievements in academics as well as life skill development.

Project Reads serves students with challenges to achieving grade-level reading by the third grade. Classroom teachers and reading interventionists refer the children who are reading below grade level. Project Reads is a one-to-one literacy tutoring program in which volunteer mentors meet weekly from September through May to help young readers improve their literacy skills. Project Reads recruits, matches, and trains volunteers in literacy techniques to stretch reading skills to meet grade-level reading benchmarks.

The JA Finance Park program begins with a teacher-taught classroom curriculum and then culminates in a visit to a capstone facility, where middle and high school students are assigned an adult "identity," complete with a family, a job, and an income. Using iPads, they then spend the day making important personal financial decisions all while maintaining a balanced budget. JA Finance Park helps students build a foundation upon which they can make intelligent financial decisions that last a lifetime.

Big Brothers Big Sisters provides quality mentoring relationships for youth in need and is based on a proven model. BBBS serves kids ages 7-21. Many are living in a single-parent household, in foster care, are low income, or have an incarcerated parent. The organization recruits, screens, trains, matches, monitors, and supports adult volunteers as one-to-one mentors for youth. The mentee and mentor meet in the community 2-4 times a month and spend time doing activities they both enjoy.

Big Brothers Big Sisters provides quality mentoring relationships for youth in need and is based on a proven model. BBBS serves kids ages 7-21. Many are living in a single-parent household, in foster care, are low income, or have an incarcerated parent. The organization recruits, screens, trains, matches, monitors, and supports adult volunteers as one-to-one mentors for youth. The mentee and mentor meet in the community 2-4 times a month and spend time doing activities they both enjoy.

The NorthStar Academic Achievement Initiative blends an innovative, team-based approach to school partnership within a Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) model: to rapidly identify NorthStar students â€“3rd-12th grade boysâ€” at-risk and furnish research-tested interventions in after-school and summer service delivery to remediate underdeveloped core educational competencies of struggling learners.

Horizons for Homeless Children operates 3 early education centers for children living in shelters in Boston. Combined they serve 175 children ages 2 months to 5 years old each day, close to 300 over the course of a year. The individualized high-quality teaching and trauma-informed approach help to mitigate the impacts of the homelessness experience and provide the children with a solid educational foundation and social/emotional skills that prepare them well for school, preventing the achievement gap that would otherwise occur.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Hampden County carefully matches  enrolled youth with a volunteer mentor. The youth often come from single parent homes, grow up in poverty, and are often coping with additional stress such as an incarcerated family member. The partnership with MassMutual supports two programs taking place throughout the academic year: The MassMutual Work Place mentoring program has significant  impact on the academic and social success of high school youth helping them plan for the future.

Career Pathways provides low literate, low-income adults with integrated educational, vocational and support services to gain employment and financial stability. While enrolled in literacy classes, students work with LVGH's Career Navigator to develop a career plan. Staff and trained volunteers provide individual and small group instruction in resume preparation, job search, interviewing and business etiquette. Students are placed through LVGH's network of engaged employers. The program also offers professional certification opportunities.

East Wayne Street Center (EWSC) administers the Project SOLVE / Family Literacy adult basic education class for individuals without a high school diploma. The program provides academic and vocational instruction and prepares students to pass the High School Equivalency Exam (HSE). Students are given work based on their academic achievement levels and tested frequently to measure their progress. Students are also given access to vocational training opportunities and pre-employment skills. Free transportation and childcare are provided.

Power Scholars Academy (PSA) is a four-week, 4.5-hours-per-day program that has intense enrichment instruction in the areas of math, literacy, and science. Students receive free breakfast, study academic lessons to improve their summer learning, have fun, and participate in field trips that support learning. PSA is currently offered at McMillan Magnet Middle School, and is a partnership with Omaha Public Schools to be the summer school program.

The Forge Skills Bootcamp goal is to empower and inspire its participants to experience a trade and pursue career paths in the trades, leading to further education, apprenticeship programs and career opportunities in a skilled trade. This will be accomplished through hands-on learning activities, access to the Forge facility, and direct access to mentoring. The Skills Bootcamp prioritizes supporting young adults 18-24, women who are un- or underemployed, those with justice served, and veterans.

The Residential and Transitional Housing Program for Adolescent Mothers provides housing and 24/7 supportive services for young moms aged 13-24 and their children. We support them to deal with trauma, return to education, and learn to live independently. The goal is to successfully transition these young families to living independently in the community. Services offered to the young families include safe housing, mental health support and counseling, onsite high school, post-secondary support, life skills programs, healthcare, and more. This report captures postnatal (length of stay 1-4 years), 55/57 Humewood (length of stay 2 years) and 1900 Sheppard (length of stay 4 years) aspects of the program.

PIE is a program of tuition grants and aid that augments what low-income families can contribute to the cost of school, thus making it possible for their children to receive an academically excellent, character-building, morally grounded education in a city Catholic school (PreK-8). Tuition grants are awarded to students who demonstrate financial need and commit to maintaining good attendance and study habits. To determine financial eligibility, the Archdiocese uses FACTS Tuition Management Company to verify family incomes and determine need.

The Trevor-Rees Jones ScoutReach program offered by the Circle Ten Council, Boy Scouts of America is our commitment to the quality delivery of a premier Scouting program in communities within our council's 24 county geographical service area for under-privileged and/or at risk youth. We want to ensure that the life-changing character building values of Scouting are available to any youth that wants to participate. Through support from ExxonMobil, we are able to provide the magic of the Scouting program to nearly 13,000 area youth each year.

The NSBE Student Retention Toolkit provides evidence-based leading practices to help  prepare and advance underrepresented students in engineering degree programs.\The briefs, a part of NSBE's broader effort to increase he number of Black scholars that go and graduate from Engineering programs, include clear action steps to effectively increase STEM proficiency and persistence.

The designated funds provide scholarships for underrepresented engineering students and continuous support facilitates a cohort cycle of student advancement  through graduation with a target of supporting 10-12 scholars total.\ \Program goals were to:  1) use the funds as a minority  retention tool, 2) fund scholar cohorts for four years in the program, 3) develop a mentoring element, 4) increase the participant graduation rate and 5) promote community engagement and service.  Each of the goals has been met with success.

GEMâ€™s fellowship programs span the entire recruitment, retention, and professional development spectrum. GEMâ€™s principal activity is the provision of graduate fellowships at the MS and PhD levels coupled with paid summer internships at a sponsoring GEM Employer. GEM also offers fellowships without paid summer internships through our GEM University and Associate Fellowship programs. Fellows are required to attend a GEM Member University, maintain satisfactory progress toward an MS or PhD degree.

The partnership with MassMutual supports two programs taking place throughout the academic year: The MassMutual Work Place mentoring program has significant  impact on the academic and social success of high school youth helping them plan for the future.

Big Brothers Big Sisters Site-Based mentoring provides students in the city of Springfield a positive role model to connect with. Mentoring activities take place during the course of a school day at the students school. Expected youth outcomes include improved attitudes towards school and school attendance as well as class participation.

The Beyond Literacy (â€œBeLitâ€) program, â€œFrom Learning to Earning: Community and Workforce Educationâ€ serves low-income adults in Philadelphia, most of whom are unemployed, underemployed or lack a high school credential. The program supports adult learners in their journey toward self-sufficiency by offering free literacy, high school equivalency test preparation, English Language Acquisition and Citizenship classes, and workforce preparation courses, as well as transition services and career counseling.

East Wayne Street Center (EWSC) administers the Project SOLVE / Family Literacy adult basic education class for individuals without a high school diploma. The program provides academic and vocational instruction and prepares students to pass the High School Equivalency Exam (HSE). Students are given work based on their academic achievement levels and tested frequently to measure their progress. Students are also given access to vocational training opportunities and pre-employment skills. Free transportation and childcare are provided.

Project STABLE provides an integrated, bundled approach to deliver industry-specific training, employment services, financial coaching, and connections to income supports to low to middle income, primarily minority, Greater Hartford residents with incomes at or below United Ways' A.L.I.C.E. â€œstability threshold. These services help participants increase household income, develop marketable skills, earn a sustainable wage, pursue a growth industry career, manage personal finances, secure sustainable income, and build financial assets.

LISCâ€™s Financial Opportunity Center (FOC) program partners with community members from underinvested neighborhoods to build family-sustaining careers and achieve financial success. Residents work side-by-side with FOC coaches to identify, make measurable progress towards and achieve their goals through connections to employment services, greater financial health, and household income support. LISC supports trusted partners to adopt the FOC model and provides them with data-based insights, technical assistance, training and peer-learning groups.

The American College Center for Military and Veterans Affairs provides applied financial knowledge, educational support, and career opportunities for military members and their families.  The Center empowers activeâ€duty, guard, reserve members, veterans, and their families with knowledge so that they can enhance their personal goals and professional careers.  Scholarships, thought leadership and research, career services, and consumer financial knowledge are all crucial to the Center's mission.

The SNAP Outreach & Enrollment program is a critical part of The Food Bank's strategy to address food insecurity by increasing households' access to healthy food. The SNAP Outreach staff works with hundreds of community sites each year to educate people and partners about SNAP eligibility and assist those in need to enroll in the program. Since the COVID pandemic began, staff has been doing SNAP enrollments exclusively over the phone.

LISCâ€™s Bridges to Career Opportunities continues to respond to community challenges in job attainment by expanding the reach of our Financial Opportunity Centers through Bridge programs. For this funding cycle, we are asking for support to continue the work of the financial and employment coaches at RCFE. In this new world following a global crisis, the barriers to job retention are ever-present and greater flexibility on behalf of the Bridge program coaches is required to support residents to meet their needs and goals.

The goal of Math Motivators is to close the opportunity gap by using a volunteer-driven math tutoring program that pairs underserved students with professionals and college students trained as tutors. We serve students in grades 3â€“12 and early college, with a focus on middle and high school students. Math Motivators has its roots in the actuarial community, but volunteers from all backgrounds are welcome.

The Financial Education Program teaches the fundamentals of personal finance. Workshops provide participants with the right tools and support to take control of their financial future. Within this program, youth that are aging out of foster care can participate in a match savings program. The goal of the Financial Education Program is to empower individuals and family to become financially stable.

Individuals who participate in CCCS's Building Financial Capability and Financial Coaching program will gain overall financial capability for themselves and their families by gaining knowledge of consumer rights and basic financial tools; learning values on money issues, budgeting, and the proper use of debt and credit; home-buying strategies; how and when to utilize Reverse Mortgages; how to avoid becoming a victim of Senior Scams and Frauds; and assistance in Foreclosure Prevention.

Collaborative effort between NNCC, partner organizations and the community. Our goal is to foster economic prosperity and improve the quality of life for residents of the North End community. By addressing key areas such as community wealth building, strong resource connections, and working towards a vibrant North End community, we aim to create lasting positive change.

Forge City Works trains individuals with barriers to employment for the culinary and customer service fields. Participants join the program in cohorts and learn soft job skills, technical culinary skills, and how to work effectively as a team. They earn minimum wage during the training, have the opportunity to intern at a job that interests them in our social enterprise, and then FCW assists them in finding and keeping a job.

The Literacy Alliance prepares adult learners for success.  Through classroom instruction and distance learning tools, adults improve academic skills, prepare for the workplace, and gain certification training.  Most come to prepare for the high school equivalency (HSE) exam. Regular assessments are given to measure progress.  Adult learners explore college and career pathways through a free online tool, Indiana Career Explorer.

The TWM Residency finds, trains, and supports BIPOC and anti-racist educators to lead in classrooms across Western Massachusetts, with the aim of diversifying the local education workforce with effective teachers reflective of their studentsâ€™ life experiences and identities. In addition to preparing early-career teachers with a pathway to success, we are focused on retaining high-quality educators. Our progressive approach and anti-oppressive practices sets us apart, as we humanize traditional teaching styles and champion educational equity.

Participants who complete CareerBridge training will receive Case Management support as needed for up to one year after completion of training. Case managers check in with course graduates at 4 weeks, 3 months, 6 months and 12 months after the course. Each participant will receive support for resume writing, interview preparation and job search assistance.  ULCC will also utilize industry-specific employer councils to align our training with industry standards for middle-skill employment.

Greater Phoenix Urban League will provide a comprehensive summer work experience for our cityâ€™s most vulnerable youth. The program is designed to build a strong foundation to assist youth in developing work ethics and guidance to a successful career path. The youth ages 16 to 24 will gain work skills and career development through summer employment and weekly workshops and trainings. Full-time employment resources and counseling will be provided for youth over 18 -24 and in need of year round employment. The program expanded its service area.

FOCs provide employment and career counseling, one-on-one financial coaching and education and low-cost financial products that help build credit, savings and assets. They also connect clients with income supports such as food stamps, utilities assistance and affordable health insurance.  The cornerstone of the FOC model is providing these services in an integrated wayâ€”rather than as stand-alone servicesâ€”and with a long-term commitment to helping clients reach their financial goals through concrete gains in net income and job retention.

The Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration (HVAC/R) Program is a comprehensive collection of lessons providing the knowledge necessary for students to understand and service HVAC/R systems in multi-family, residential, and commercial buildings. The program is led by training partner Occupancy Heroes and offers students opportunities to complete necessary certification exams. During the four-week program, students practice skills on custom-built simulators and learn on-the-job with instructors.

Employment Specialists meet with clients to determine interests and skill. Potential job sites, that offer positions consistent with the client's interests and skills are identified. Clients receive assistance completing employment applications and interviews. Intensive job coaching is provided for the first several weeks of employment, assisting the client in learning job tasks and providing support for the client and employer. Intensive assistance is phased out and replaced with ongoing, long-term support in maintaining employment.

TFA Massachusetts is a local teaching corps dedicated to recruiting, training, and supporting recent college graduates and professionals to teach in high-need communities and bolster the effort for educational equity across the Commonwealth. With extensive training and support, corps members, work relentlessly to lead students to dramatic academic growth for two years. TFA corps members become alumni - many of whom continue working in classrooms, school, and the broader education ecosystem to improve educational inequity.

As part of Frayser Connect, Epicenter focuses on stimulating entrepreneurship as a means to increased personal and community wealth, as well as increasing the economic impact of growing, profitable small businesses. Epicenter uses a range of small business supports, customized technical assistance, and a  spectrum of flexible financing tools and resources to help entrepreneurs and business owners create, build, and sustain their businesses.

The UL Black Business Support Initiative strives to engage, elevate and empower Black Businesses in the Greater Springfield area by providing business support services and access to entrepreneurship education to grow, scale and produce sustainable businesses.  The UL will work with a cohort of  businesses who will be assigned specific training opportunities distinct to their business growth needs.  Workshops and Forums will also be held  to showcase successful entrepreneurs who will provide insight and perspective of good business practices.

The #GreenNFit Neighborhood Rebuild and Springfield Healthy Homes Program compliment each other. The project repairs/rehabilitates up to 20 homes to improve energy-efficiency, safety, accessibility and health in a neighborhood with the help of 1,000 volunteers. In partnership, the national Green & Healthy Homes Initiative, Baystate Health, and the Public Health Institute/Pioneer Valley Asthma Coalition pool their expertise in an evidence-based asthma home-visiting and environmental intervention.

City Connects is an integrated student support intervention. Its mission is to help children succeed and thrive by connecting each student with a tailored set of services in the school and community. At the core is a Coordinator in each school, a school counselor or social worker, who works with each classroom teacher to review every student and develop customized support plans addressing strengths and needs across developmental domains (academic, social-emotional/behavioral, health, family), then connect students with services and enrichments.

FutureSmart is a digital education course designed specifically for middle school students to increase the learner's knowledge about financial literacy, their confidence in their own skills, their ability to interact with financial products, and the likelihood to engage in financial conversations about plans for the future with peers, adults, and parents.

Math Motivators SAT/ACT and AP Test Prep program offering pairs underserved high school students with volunteers who are math experts in STEM fields and trained as tutors by our team of educational professionals.

PIE is a program of tuition grants and aid that augments what low-income families can contribute to the cost of school, thus making it possible for their children to receive an academically excellent, character-building, morally grounded education in a city Catholic school (PreK-8). Tuition grants are awarded to students who demonstrate financial need and commit to maintaining good attendance and study habits. To determine financial eligibility, the Archdiocese uses FACTS Tuition Management Company to verify family incomes and determine need.

A cornerstone teacher pipeline partner for Baltimore City Public Schools operating since 2010, Urban Teachers recruits, prepares, develops, and supports the retention of diverse career educators to improve academic and life outcomes for PreK-12 students in our city. Following strategic recruitment, we provide multiple years of practice-based programming for aspiring and new teachers (including a yearlong pre-teaching residency) and tie dual certification in general *and* special education to success in the classroom and our program over time.

The Roof Replacement program provides roof replacements to low income senior homeowners that live within the City of Atlanta. The program is funded through our partnership with the City of Atlanta. The program's primary objectives is to improve the health, safety, and energy savings for senior homeowners  that would not be able to stay in their home if not for the services.

The program provides coverage for direct dental costs for low income, un-insured or under-insured individuals. The program provides comprehensive dental care to adults and children by providing Delta Dental grant funds to cover the patient costs for dental procedures.

San JosÃ© Clinic (SJC) has served the greater Houston community as a stable dental home for local uninsured, underserved patients for the past 101 years. SJC's dental clinic historically provides more than 6,000 visits to approximately 1,500 patients annually. 78% of patients at San JosÃ© Clinic are Hispanic, and many prefer to speak Spanish, so all of the frontline staff members are bilingual in Spanish and English. The dental clinic provides preventative and restorative dental care, including extractions and implants.

AHSâ€™ Dental Clinic serves over 7,700 patients annually at six dental sites (three fixed and three school-based programs). AHSâ€™ Dental Program provides culturally and linguistically appropriate quality oral health care to the predominantly low-income Asian and Pacific Islander (API) population in Alameda County. AHSâ€™ Dental Program also provides full scope dental care in four oral health specialties (pediatric dentistry, endodontics, periodontics, and oral surgery).

Located in Central Texas, Lone Star Circle of Care at Marble Falls is the only Federally Qualified Health Center serving Burnet County, Texas. This clinic site provides dental care to more than 600 patients annually. Apart from LSCC, there are few affordable, sliding fee scale options for an uninsured patient in need of dental services in this rural county.  Dental services are provided to self-pay, low-income patients at a reasonable charge; however, no patient is ever refused services based on inability to pay.

Project HOMEâ€™s Healthcare Services provide medical, dental, and behavioral health services for a population that is underserved - persons who have experienced homelessness, as well as low-income adults and children living in Lower North Philadelphia. Patients are typically uninsured or underinsured, with limited access to care at traditional healthcare settings. Dental staff help patients practice preventative care, screen for major oral diseases, and engage in the critical care they require to attain and retain good health.

Dental services are a core component of Mary's Center's holistic, multipronged approach to care. Mary's Center's award-winning dental services fill a crucial gap in care for our communities. Our offices provide safe and comprehensive preventative and restorative dental care to an under-resourced population who are often medically complex or at a high risk for complications. Our dental clinics attract a significant number of participants from Maryland, where safety-net dental insurance coverage is scant.

Grady's Oral Health Center ensures that more than 2,000 people living with advanced HIV receive comprehensive oral health care. The Oral Health Center is the only place in metro Atlanta offering a full range of preventative, restorative, and prosthetic dental services exclusively to low-income patients living with HIV/AIDS. The Oral Health Center is staff by a team of dental professionals with deep expertise meeting the complex needs of patients living with HIV, who are at a much higher risk for oral health problems.
Whitman-Walker offers a full range of dental services, including both preventative and restorative oral care. A general dental exam helps you understand your overall dental health and hygiene.

The North East Medical Services (NEMS) Dental Program consists of six dental clinics located in the San Francisco Bay Area, annually serving approximately 16,000 patients through roughly 45,000 visits. NEMS provides comprehensive, linguistically competent and culturally sensitive health care, including dental care, to a variety of patients, a majority of whom are low-income, immigrant Asians. Overall, NEMS provides comprehensive health care services to over 67,000 patients annually.

This program helps to foster a high level of oral care by aiding in the diagnosis of dental conditions and the preparation of  treatment planning. As a result, it improves quality of care, health equity, and patient outcomes among our FQHC's diverse patient population.

Earth Tech is a national six-month accelerator for early-stage climate and water technology solutions that positively impact communities and ecosystems across Canada. Each year, the program offers about 15 startups and nonprofit social enterprises mentorship and advising, training, community and peer support, and access to investors, funders and experts in order to validate their solutions and business models, advance their technology readiness, and create meaningful environmental impact.

Vista Community Clinic (VCC) cares for over 5,700 diabetic patients out of a patient population of 68,000. This program has identified patients with diabetes who are at risk of oral and eye health problems and ensures that they are evaluated for, educated about, and when needed treated for the oral and eye diseases that diabetes can cause. VCC has added an integration coordinator, trained staff, printed educational materials for patients, and distributed care kits in an effort to provide whole person care.

The NEVHC Dental Program offers low-cost, quality and comprehensive preventive and restorative oral health services for low-income, underserved and predominantly Latinx residents of Los Angeles County's San Fernando and Santa Clarita valleys. More specifically, NEVHC operates 39 dental operatories across 7 dental clinic sites, which, in calendar year 2022, provided 18,818 patients with 49,524 dental visits. NEVHC also offers pediatric preventive oral health screenings and referrals for 6,216 youth at primary care sites in Pacoima and Van Nuys.

Each year, Special Olympics CT hosts an Annual Summer Games competition and Health screening event. Athletes from around the state have the opportunity to come together and compete in the sports of: soccer, swimming, tennis, cycling, race-walking, track and field. In addition, there is a Healthy Athletes venue where athletes can receive free health screenings in 6 different disciplines.  Through the event, athletes work to inspire the message that people with intellectual disabilities are capable, gifted, & vital members of society.

The Pediatric Dentistry department at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry provides a dental home for children ages 0-17 who participate in the Oral Health for all Underserved Uninsured Program (OH-UUC). The program's purpose is to reduce the number of uninsured and underserved children living in Baltimore with untreated caries and shift the focus to preventative services for maintaining oral health.

Founded in 1971, La ClÃ­nica de La Raza, Inc. (La ClÃ­nica) is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that provides comprehensive health care to underserved populations in Alameda, Contra Costa, and Solano Counties. Eleven (11) of La ClÃ­nicaâ€™s 35 service sites provide dental services, including four-school based sites, six fixed sites, and one mobile van. Additionally, La ClÃ­nicaâ€™s Oral Health Initiative uses portable dental equipment to provide community-based dental services and oral health education to children in school settings.

JA BizTown is a unique experiential education program featuring twelve teacher-led lessons in the classroom and culminating with an immersion in a simulated town at the JACC headquarters. Sixth grade students operate businesses, manage their finances, vote for mayor, and make choices that require collaboration and critical thinking.  JA Biztown helps students connect the dots between what they learn in school and the real world.

The Workforce Financial Counseling program pairs unemployed or underemployed beneficiaries with a certified financial counselor to provide one-on-one personal finance assistance. Beneficiaries, sourced in partnership with Philadelphia Works from CareerLink sites, can use the service as often as they'd like. Counselors help beneficiaries navigate steps for improving credit scores, create budgets, and set personal financial goals.

Caridad Center, founded in 1989, has evolved over the past 30 years from a modest trailer in rural Palm Beach County dispensing free medical treatment for migrant farmworkers to the largest free clinic in Florida. Caridad Center's Dental Clinic offers comprehensive services, including dental screening, hygiene, treatment, and oral health education.

Catholic Charities of Central Florida operates free dental clinics that provide quality dental care to uninsured and underserved men and women who are living at or below 200% of the poverty level. The clinics are located in federally designated Health Professional Shortage Areas where access to care is difficult even for the insured. Catholic Charities recruits volunteer dentists, hygienists, and assistants to provide hundreds of free visits each year. The current emphasis is on opening more locations to further increase access.

Bread for the Cityâ€™s Dental Clinic offers uninsured and underinsured individuals and families all of the services they need to properly maintain oral health: cleanings, fillings, x-rays, extractions, root canals, and more. In addition, we provide education and support to dental care patients regarding proper oral health, encouraging effective brushing, flossing, and gum care. Each patient receives an oral health care kit at each visit, and follow-ups ensure that patients visit the clinic on a regular basis for proper monitoring.

JA Finance Park teaches key concepts about personal finance, budgeting, credit, and building a foundation for solid financial decision making.  Students in grades 8-12 prepare by having 17 classroom lessons before visiting JA's simulation site where students develop and manage a personal budget based on a given persona for the day.  Trained volunteers lead students through a 4.5 hour simulation where they use critical thinking and decision-making skills, and learn lifelong lessons and options, choices, career pathways, and financial literacy.

The primary focus of the Community Dentistry program is to provide quality, affordable, and accessible dental services to the underserved and uninsured children, especially those in rural non-fluoridated communities who might not otherwise receive care.  It provides free dental screenings and dental health and nutrition education to students in nearly 200 schools and Head Starts across upstate NY, as well as an oral health toolkit at no cost to the family. Additional preventative services are provided to children that enroll.

Our Dientes Cares Program focuses on making oral health care accessible for low-income, uninsured patients. Dientes offers affordable sliding scale fees for those without insurance and free care through our uncompensated care fund for those who need it most. To increase access to care, we keep these fees affordable by fundraising to subsidize costs.

Unity offers a robust dental program targeting low income, uninsured and underserved segment of the District of Columbia population . Its Dental Department  currently provides preventative and specialty oral health services at 9 community sites across the District including the DC Jail and two school based health centers. It also works closely with pediatricians and other child health care practitioners to promote oral health screenings during well-child visits.

The Susan Dew Hoff Memorial Clinic operates year-round to offer free-or-reduced-fee dental services to the working poor, to cancer patients and to disenfranchised veterans in Harrison County, WV. The clinic's goal is to relieve pain and restore the oral cavity to as many people as resources allow. Susan Dew Hoff receives no government funding; instead, it relies on grants and donations.

Neighborhood Health Center of WNY delivers impactful healthcare provided by kind people so that Western New Yorkers can achieve their dreams and goals. NHC's Dental Department provides quality care to all persons, regardless of their ability to pay. Integrating oral health into the primary care setting enhances access and patient outcomes for some of Western New York's most vulnerable populations.

The Manos Dental Center delivers affordable emergency, restorative, and preventative oral healthcare services to the underserved population of Central Texas. Patients are charged approximately thirty percent of the market rates in conventional offices within the zip code region. Distinguishing itself as one of Austin's only full-service dental centers, Manos boasts a remarkable 35-year history as a safety net clinic.

The C. L. Brumback Primary Care Clinics provide preventive dental services to adults and children throughout Palm Beach County. These sites can be found in West Palm Beach, Lantana, Delray Beach, and Belle Glade. Costs for dental services are based on a patientâ€™s family size and income and all patients will be served whether or not they are insured.

The Care for Kids Program (CFK) ensures that children living in Montgomery County who do not qualify for the Maryland Childrenâ€™s Health Program (MCHIP) or Medical Assistance and whose families have incomes under 250% of the Federal Poverty Level have access to primary and specialty health care services. CFK is a partnership among the Primary Care Coalition, Montgomery County DHHS, School-Based Health and Wellness Centers, Kaiser Permanente, non-profit clinics, and private health care providers.

Project SERVE is a job training and community revitalization program which provides returning citizens and unemployed or underemployed individuals with the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully find and sustain full-time employment. Program goals are to train and place participants in sustainable living-wage employment, provide supportive services to eliminate barriers to success, prevent recidivism, and meet the diverse range of needs of returning citizens.

The CDHC is a non-profit comprehensive dental home and teaching program. Our urban, hospital-adjacent main facility is housed on the campus of the Miller Children's & Women's Hospital in Long Beach, CA. Our rural, school-based clinic is housed on the campus the Avalon School on the rural community of Santa Catalina Island. We are the safety-net oral health provider for 5,500 underserved and medically compromised children and young adults (0-21) in greater Long Beach and on Santa Catalina Island.

DAP Health provides oral healthcare services to low-income, under insured, and uninsured community members at the DAP main campus. The Dental Clinic offers a broad spectrum of preventative and restorative oral healthcare procedures to patients. Delaying preventative dental care due to economic disadvantage not only risks a patientâ€™s health but also ultimately results in higher cost of late stage intervention. Services are provided on a sliding fee scale depending on individual client income eligibility.

The Gateway Community Health Center Inc., (Gateway) Lado A Lado Dental Program provides adults over 22 years of age, access to proper dental services. The Adult Dental Services Program, absorbs the preventative and restorative direct dental healthcare costs for each qualifying patent. This enables patients suffering through great financial need, to receive dental services at no cost to them.

EXCELth, Inc. is dedicated to improving the health of underserved New Orleans and Baton Rouge communities by bringing high-quality, affordable primary care to everyone who needs it regardless of their ability to pay. Comprehensive dental care is provided on a sliding scale for uninsured persons at two fixed sites. Two mobile dental units serve students, senior centers and developmentally disabled  persons. EXCELth is also a leader in improving oral health throughout the State by promoting teledentistry, and creating AEGD residency programs.

TCDC is solely focused on ensuring access and providing dental care to children who are enrolled in Medi-Cal Dental, are underinsured and families requiring a sliding scale fee structure to make dental care affordable. We opened our doors in 2003 and have become a trusted, reliable dental home for thousands of children. Our talented clinical team is skilled at delivering care to children and they are supported by a compassionate group of auxiliary staff.

LCH Health and Community Services is a nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) providing affordable, high quality health care to low income residents of southern Chester County, Pennsylvania.  Since its start, LCH has served a primarily Latino patient population and is completely bilingual and bicultural.  Since opening its Dental Center in 2018, LCH has offered quality dental services to more than 1,500 unduplicated individuals a year, fully integrated with primary health and pediatric care.

The Kids Smiles Promise Zone Program provides essential oral health care, outreach services, and educational programming to children and families residing in the West Philadelphia Promise Zone. Kids Smiles partners with CHOP Early Head Start, Brightside Academy, and other early learning centers to reach children and parents/caregivers with dental resources to help them begin and maintain a healthy oral health routine. The program aims to expand access to care and increase health literacy for children and families in the Promise Zone.

Open Door Family Medical Center's Dental Care Program provides high quality primary care to deeply underserved and vulnerable populations in New York's Hudson Valley.  Access for these populations is bolstered by convenient locations, expanded hours, and a bilingual staff that is familiar with both the social determinants of health faced by their patients and the resources needed to empower their health.  Five permanent Open Door dental locations and a mobile van spread across three counties serve 20,000 unique patients a year.

Coastal Family Health Center offers oral health services to patients eligible for Health Care for the Homeless Program at no cost to the patient. These services consist of reviewing oral health history, performing a physical examination, completing X-rays, referring for preventative dental care treatment and performing sealants, fillings and extractions, as needed.

Fourth Street Clinic dental program serves men and women in Salt Lake County experiencing homelessness.  A full array of services are available at little ($1.00 - $4.00) to no cost.  Individuals have access to restorative dental care (including dentures), preventative dental cleanings and education, emergency and routine dental care.

Salt Lake Donated Dental Services' (SLDDS) community dental project aims to relieve dental pain and suffering while preserving oral health through preventive education and comprehensive treatment for those with no other access to care. The target population is patients living within 0-200% of the Federal Poverty Level, which includes people of all ages, genders, and backgrounds, patients with disabilities, experiencing homelessness or struggling with substance abuse, refugees, immigrants, veterans, and victims of domestic violence.

Miami FL,-  has seen an increase in the percentage of persons who report that cost associated with oral health related visits is a barrier to accessing care, showcasing the need for service providers as JTCHS who serve persons regardless of ability to pay. During this untimely Pandemic JTCHS continues to be the provider of choice for the community. With the allocation of grant funds, JTCHS will have the ability to continue to deliver quality oral health services (preventive, emergency, restorative, rehabilitative) to patients & their families.
